name: The Messiah
plain_explanation: The hope for a future deliverer who would set things right for the chosen people.
precise_definition: For Jews, a future figure who would bring temporal prosperity and victory over enemies on earth; for Christians, this hope was historicized and identified with Jesus, also merged with the Greek philosophical idea of the Logos, and relocated to a heavenly rather than earthly triumph.
why_it_mattered: It shows the transformation of a this-worldly Jewish political hope into an other-worldly Christian theological doctrine.
historical_origin: Rooted in prophetic texts, especially those of Deutero-Isaiah, later read by Christians as predictions of Christ.
examples: Isaiah's prophecies of the 'Prince of Peace' and the suffering servant of Isaiah 53
influence_on_later_thinkers: Central to Christian theology from the outset (Chapter II).
connection_to_politics_or_religion: Originally a political hope for national deliverance, later theologized.

evolution.treatment: The hope for a future deliverer who would set things right for the chosen people.
